name: Blue Is Glue
price: Free to register, about $11 a year
story: In Mission: Impossible Ghost Protocol, Tom Cruise climbs the outside of the Burj Khalifa on suction gloves. He gets one instruction: blue is glue, red is dead. He hung off the real tower to film it. This is the Bending Spoons move with a Dubai address: a film scene about doing the impossible, shot on the building you see every day. And blue is already your colour.

name: Still See The Sun
price: Free to register, about $11 a year
story: The Burj Khalifa is so tall that the sun sets later at the top. In 2011 Dubai's clerics ruled that people living above floor 80 must break the Ramadan fast two minutes later, and above floor 150 three minutes later, because up there they can still see the sun. Build high enough and you get more daylight than everyone else.

name: Back Of The Fence
price: Free to register, about $11 a year
story: Paul Jobs taught his son Steve to build the back of a fence as carefully as the front, even though nobody would ever see it. You will know it is there, he said. Steve later demanded the same of the circuit boards inside the first Mac. A name for people who finish the part no user sees.

name: Wrong Kind Of Sand
price: Free to register, about $11 a year
story: The UAE sits in a desert and still imports sand. Desert grains are blown round and smooth by the wind, so they cannot hold concrete together. The towers were built with rougher sand brought in from elsewhere. Having a lot of something is not the same as having the right thing. Funny, true, and hard to forget.

name: Two Leased Planes
price: Free to register, about $11 a year
story: Emirates took off on 25 October 1985 with 10 million dollars and two planes leased from Pakistan's national airline. Today it is one of the biggest airlines in the world. The whole Dubai story in three words: start with what you can borrow, then build something nobody can ignore.

name: Signed Inside
price: Free to register, about $11 a year
story: In 1982 the team that built the first Macintosh signed a sheet of paper. Steve Jobs had the signatures moulded into the inside of every case, where no customer would ever look, because real artists sign their work. A name for a company that puts its name on everything it ships, even the parts nobody opens.

name: Luck Of Lucks
price: Free to register, about $11 a year
story: Most bright stars still carry the names Arab astronomers gave them. One of them is Sadalsuud, which means luck of lucks. It rose with the sun when winter ended and the good season began. Like 37signals, it is a name taken from the sky. Unlike it, the story comes from this part of the world.

name: Sheep In A Box
price: Free to register, about $11 a year
story: In The Little Prince, a pilot crashes in the desert and a boy asks him to draw a sheep. Three drawings fail. So he draws a box with air holes and says the sheep is inside. The boy is delighted: it is exactly the sheep he wanted. A desert story about products that leave room for the imagination.

name: Confuse The Wind
price: Free to register, about $11 a year
story: A tower as tall as the Burj Khalifa should be shaken apart by the wind. Its engineer, Bill Baker, explained why it is not: we confuse the wind. Every setback gives the tower a different shape, so the wind never gets organised against it. A name about beating a huge force with design, not with muscle.

name: Penguins Upstairs
price: Free to register, about $11 a year
story: Inside the Mall of the Emirates, a short walk from the shops, lives a colony of king and gentoo penguins. In a desert city where summer passes 45 degrees. Nobody finds it strange any more. This is the Mustard and Linen kind of name: ridiculous, true, and a reminder that here somebody always says yes to the idea.
